clauses.requirement: The rear lamp, as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) containing LED modules on a PCB, shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation using the test method(s) described in UN R10 Annex 9.
The general provisions of UN R10 Annex 9 (paragraph 1) shall be applied to the immunity testing of the rear lamp ESA.
The test method(s) described in UN R10 Annex 9 shall be applied to the rear lamp as an ESA.

The Annex 9 test methods shall be applied to both kinds of ESA: (a) ESAs other than those involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid'; (b) ESAs involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid'; the applicable kind shall be determined for the rear lamp.

The rear lamp ESA may comply using any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of: (a) absorber chamber test per ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing per ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing per ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing per ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test per ISO 11452-11; provided the combination covers the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9; ESAs in configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' shall comply using the combination of absorber chamber test per ISO 11452-2 and bulk current injection testing per ISO 11452-4, at the manufacturer's discretion, covering the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1; frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The state of the rear lamp ESA during the immunity tests shall be as specified in UN R10 Annex 9 paragraph 2.
The immunity test conditions for the rear lamp ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.

During the tests the rear lamp ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, and shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
